About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.7% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

About the Team

Our internship program is structured to provide interns with the opportunity to work on real projects that our customers urgently need. In this role you will be part of the Product Design team, which is made up of several groups that define, create, and deliver all user-facing aspects of Stripe’s product. Product Designers are strategic partners to Engineering and Product Management within their product area. In close collaboration with product teams, they shape user experiences, then translate them into high-quality designs that can be tested, shipped, and refined. Designers are responsible for building elegant, functional products that users love—and want to tell others about.

What You'll Do

As a Product Design Intern, you will focus on designing and building experiences that will be shipped to our users in production. You will contribute design iterations to ongoing project workstreams, tackling important projects to increase global commerce, and help shape brand new experiences. Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high. 

Key responsibilities include:

  • Work on a product design project with a product team, translating business ideas into real experience.
  • Help craft thoughtful experiences that enable startups and large businesses to establish and manage their businesses.
  • Apply problem-solving skills and human-centered approaches to address complex and ambiguous business and user problems.
  • Develop and refine design solutions by partnering closely with other designers.
  • Craft and prototype visually polished experiences to get user feedback. 
  • Partner closely with engineering to implement a feature/product from design to implementation, and get it in the hands of our users.
  • Engage in group design critiques and collaborative design sessions to improve and receive feedback on your work.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders, including engineers, product managers, data scientists, and researchers, proactively seeking and incorporating feedback.
  • Understand and advocate for our users, participating in the design process from early concepts to final delivery.

Who You Are

  • Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
  • Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. 
  • Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.

Minimum Requirements

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a design-related field, such as UX/UI, Interaction Design, Human Interface, Computer Science,  HCI, or a related discipline.
  • Some experience using computer programs to design, such as Figma/Canva.
  • Demonstrated experience designing experiences and user flows.
  • Strong understanding of user-centered design principles and best practices.
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems, form an understanding through independent research, and effectively work with a mentor and teammates.
  • Are a self-motivated problem solver committed to personal growth.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate work while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs.
  • Ability to participate in a paid full-time internship between May–August, 2027. 

Preferred Qualifications (A bonus, not a requirement)

  • Previous project, internship, or work experience in UX/UI design or related fields.
  • Experience working with or conducting your own research, presenting results, and acting on those results.
  • Experience with AI tools like Cursor, Lovable, V0, or any others.
  • Strong knowledge in design craft and visual design.
  • Intent to return to the degree program after the completion of the internship/co-op.

Company Description

About us

Solflare is a Solana self-custody wallet that puts people in control of their digital assets. Around 4 million users control $20 billion in funds through our wallet.

What started as a team of 6 in 2020 building Solana's first wallet, has grown into a team of 150 worldwide. We’re remote-first, but if you happen to stop by in Zagreb, Croatia, or Belgrade or Novi Sad, Serbia, we have an office you can work from if that’s what you prefer. 

Wherever we work, we share the same goal: a Web3 wallet for everyone, with financial freedom in their hands.

Job Description

The role

This is not a testing role in the traditional sense. We're not looking for someone to catch bugs at the end of the pipeline and hand them back. We're looking for someone to own how quality happens across the entire product. As we like to put it: QA owns the testing strategy, not product quality. Product quality is shared by Product and Engineering.

Your job is to make sure the whole system is set up so that everyone can build confidence in what we ship, from the moment a feature is designed to the moment it's released. That means enabling engineers to test effectively, driving a quality mindset across teams, and building the systems and processes that support it, not just writing and running test cases.

We think about quality the way our users experience the product: as complete journeys, not as a checklist of acceptance criteria. If you read this and think "quality is someone else's problem once I've logged the bug," this role isn't for you. If you think in terms of "can the user actually achieve their goal here, and how do I make the whole team confident that they can," keep reading.

This is a senior role because it demands ownership. Not the word, the behavior: seeing what needs to happen and making it happen without being told, working across Product, Engineering, Data as a matter of course, and taking responsibility for the testing strategy of a feature end to end.

Core responsibilities

  • Own the testing strategy for the features and areas you work on. Decide how confidence gets built, which validation happens at which layer (unit, component, integration, API, golden, E2E, accessibility, performance, security, manual, exploratory), rather than defaulting everything to end-to-end testing.
  • Get involved early. Join discovery and specification reviews before development starts: clarify assumptions, surface edge cases, identify risks and dependencies, and ask the hard questions ("what happens if the API fails, if permissions are denied, if the user abandons the flow?").
  • Design test cases as part of feature development, not after it. Covering user journeys, happy paths, edge cases, error handling, recovery, and regression.
  • Enable engineers to own their part of quality. Give developers the test suites, regression packs, environments, and mock data they need to validate their own work before it reaches you, and help build a culture where they do.
  • Do the testing that matters. Structured execution of prepared cases plus mandatory exploratory testing to find what predefined cases can't predict, like usability issues, cross-feature interactions, and wrong assumptions.
  • Maintain a living view of test coverage per feature. So release decisions are based on measurable confidence rather than "the ticket is closed."
  • Continuously improve the automation strategy and the process itself. Reduce flakiness, close coverage gaps, cut repetitive manual regression, and free up time for exploratory, accessibility, security, and performance work.
  • Bring AI/LLM tools into the workflow. Use them to speed up test case design, automation scripting, and exploratory testing, and keep pushing the team's QA practices forward as new tools emerge.

 

 

Qualifications

Requirements: 

  • A minimum of a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • Senior level experience in QA. You've owned quality for real features or products, made your own calls on testing strategy, and been accountable for the outcome, not just executed test plans someone else wrote.
  • A genuine ownership and proactivity mindset. You spot gaps and close them, you drive things rather than wait to be assigned, and you don't treat quality as "done" the moment a bug is filed.
  • A user- and product-first way of thinking. You test journeys and business outcomes, not just acceptance criteria, and you keep the user at the center of every decision about what and how to test.
  • Security mindset.
  • Comfort with the "shift-left" idea: quality is built throughout development, not verified at the end.
  • Hands-on experience with automation tools such as WebdriverIO, Patrol, Selenium, Cypress, Appium, or Playwright.
  • Experience writing backend tests (API, unit, database) and testing RESTful services with tools such as Postman or similar
  • Experience with CI/CD platforms such as Jenkins or GitHub Actions.
  • We prioritise strong automation skills, but if your background is mostly manual, a proactive attitude, a solid technical base, and a real drive to pick up automation quickly - will still get our attention.

Nice to have: 

  • Experience in web3 or fintech, or anywhere you've tested products that handle real money. When money is on the line, there's no room for "probably fine," so it sharpens your attention to detail and your instinct for edge cases in a way that carries over well here.
  • Experience with testing across multiple layers (API, integration, golden/screenshot, performance, accessibility).
  • Experience with security testing

Additional Information

You might not like it here…

But you might love it. Working at Solflare comes with trade-offs, and we’re open about them.

Crypto moves fast, and our priorities can shift with it. We launch new features and rethink existing projects as our users’ needs evolve, in bull and bear markets alike. That means a project you expected to work on may give way to a more pressing priority. We understand this can be energizing if you can adapt and reset as you go, and frustrating if you prefer long-term predictability.

We also highly rate how people work together. Yes, individual work matters, but so does helping others succeed. We share responsibility for the outcome, and we share credit for the wins.

Our remote-first setup gives you flexibility over how you work. It also means owning your role and proactively communicating with your team, not waiting for check-ins or constant direction.

A Web3 background isn’t a must, but interest in Solflare and the industry is. Using the product, asking questions, and contributing ideas is part of every role.

You don’t have to prefer this setup. But understanding it should help you decide whether you’d enjoy working here.

 


Millions already use what we build. Help shape what comes next. Apply below, or check out our careers site to learn more about our culture and benefits.

About Kamino

Kamino's mission is to create liquidity and utility for every asset. We want the world's best investments to be available through the financial platforms people already trust, and we want investors to be able to borrow against what they own when they need liquidity, instead of having to sell.

Today, the most valuable assets in the world are often the least useful to own. Trillions of dollars sit in private markets, behind high minimums and holding periods that can run for years. Tokenization is starting to move these assets onto shared, programmable infrastructure, but putting an asset onchain is only the first step. To be useful, it still needs distribution, compliance, servicing, credit and liquidity.

Kamino already runs the credit and liquidity engine at scale. It is the largest credit protocol on Solana and the largest credit platform for real-world assets onchain, with more than $650 billion in cumulative transaction volume and more than $20 billion in loans originated.

Now we are building the rest of that system for institutions. Kamino recently named Yieldstreet co-founder Michael Weisz as CEO and is building a new HQ in New York, alongside the asset managers and financial platforms that will shape this market. Almost none of that market exists yet, and we intend to build it.

The opportunity

As Kamino expands from a team of about 50 people globally and builds a new HQ in New York, where the CEO will be based, his time has become one of the company's scarcest resources. We are looking for an Executive Assistant to be his partner: someone focused on making the CEO as successful as he can be and giving him as much operating leverage as possible.

In practice, that means thinking critically about how the CEO spends his time, making sure he is available for what matters most and taking as much off his plate as you can. You will become deeply embedded in the CEO’s day-to-day, learning his priorities, working style and relationships well enough to anticipate what he needs and act as a trusted extension of him. You will learn his voice well enough to handle most routine correspondence yourself and decide what truly needs his attention. The work runs from board updates and leadership meetings to the small things that keep him focused, and all of it serves the same aim. You will also lead the setup of Kamino's New York office.

This is not a back-office support role. Kamino runs its operations with AI agents that draft, schedule, brief and follow up. You will direct that support, check its work and supply the judgment it can't.

What you get

  • A front-row seat to a new market. You will see Kamino work with asset managers, financial platforms, investors and regulators to build what comes after tokenization, where Wall Street meets onchain finance.

  • A hand in building Kamino New York. As one of the first members of the New York team, you will find and open the office, shape how it runs and help the team grow.

  • Skills few people have yet. You will learn to run an executive office alongside AI agents, a way of working most companies have not reached.

  • Strong pay. You will be paid respectfully, with attractive upside.

What you'll do

Calendar, inbox and the CEO's voice

  • Own the CEO's calendar across time zones: scheduling, prioritization, preparation time and protected time for the most important work. When it can't all fit, know which meetings can move, lay out the trade-offs and get his decision.

  • Manage a high-volume inbox. Answer routine correspondence directly in the CEO's voice and bring him only what he needs to see, flagged as needing a decision, his input or just his awareness.

  • Hold two short check-ins with the CEO each day covering what came in, what needs a decision and what moved.

  • Triage inbound requests, including media, podcasts, speaking invitations and introductions, and route each one to the CEO, communications or the right team.

Board and leadership meetings

  • Prepare board presentations and board meetings, including the CEO's quarterly updates to the foundation board.

  • Own the agendas for management, leadership and staff meetings. Follow up with contributors about 24 hours ahead, so each meeting starts with a full agenda and the right materials.

  • Coordinate investor and partner meetings and prepare the CEO for each one: who he is meeting, the goal, the agenda and any presentations.

  • Record decisions and action items with an owner and a date, then follow each one through to completion across the team. Do the same for the approvals, signatures and introductions that run through the CEO.

Briefs, drafts and the CEO's writing

  • Keep the CEO's weekly priorities list current and build his daily, weekly and monthly briefs around it.

  • Draft investor and partner materials and other documents for the CEO's review.

  • Over time, run the CEO's blog and drafting process: review drafts, check that they make sense, act on his voice-note feedback and make sure the right people see them.

Travel and client entertainment

  • Plan domestic and international travel and client entertainment end to end, from itineraries and reservations to backup plans and expense reporting. Think ahead about how each trip affects the CEO's schedule and preparation, and adjust in real time when plans change.

  • Lead the search for Kamino's New York office with the CEO. Negotiate the commercial terms, then get the space furnished and set up.

Relationships and stakeholder management

  • Build trusted relationships with colleagues, investors, partners and other external stakeholders, serving as a reliable point of contact on the CEO’s behalf.

  • Keep those relationships moving: coordinate outreach and meetings, manage follow-ups, keep relationship records current in our CRM and know when the CEO needs to engage directly.

AI-native operations

  • Work every day with the AI agents that support the Office of the CEO. Direct their work, verify their outputs and own the quality of the result.

  • Build and improve practical AI workflows, lightweight agents and useful tools for recurring work, such as investor meeting preparation, relationship tracking and follow-ups.

  • Identify where automation saves time, test that it works reliably and apply judgment about what still needs human review.

Confidentiality and discretion

  • Handle confidential and market-sensitive information, including information about KMNO, with complete discretion and in line with Kamino's confidentiality and trading policies. Treat the CEO's personal information with the same care.

  • Maintain accurate, well-organized records and document systems for the Office of the CEO.

What success looks like

Within the first 90 days

  • The CEO's calendar and travel are fully in your hands, with a daily and weekly planning rhythm in place.

  • You handle most routine correspondence in the CEO's voice, with a clear rule for what goes to him.

  • The twice-daily check-in runs reliably, so nothing important waits without the CEO knowing.

Why this role matters

Each week the CEO works across partners, investors, regulators and a growing team in several time zones. Separating the important from the urgent is critical to helping a business grow, and in this role you will do it with him every day. You will see that impact up close, multiply the CEO's time and shape how the Office of the CEO works as Kamino grows.

A senior, trusted partner and operator. You have already shown, over years with a high-performing CEO, that you can keep a demanding executive's work moving.

  • Experience supporting board and investor relationships.

How we will work

Who we are:

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our culture:

  • We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.

  • We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

  • We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.

Location:

  • Remote - United States

The role

Sardine makes risk and payment decisions for banks and fintechs. Our customers audit us closely, and application security is a large part of what they examine.

Money moves through this platform, so real adversaries study it. Your job is to find what they would find, especially authorization flaws and business logic abuse, and then make the whole class of bug go away.

The application security team is small. The estate is large: Go, Node.js, Python, Ruby, and Java services running on multi-cloud and Kubernetes. That ratio shapes the work. Findings arrive from scanners, code review, testing, threat modeling, pentesters, and bug bounty hunters. You turn that stream into a pipeline that validates, routes, and closes issues with as little manual effort as possible. Then you use what the pipeline tells you to remove root causes: secure defaults, patterns engineers reach for first, and fixes that hold.

Little here is pre-decided. You determine where the risk is and go after it.

The work

Where most of your time goes

Running and automating the vulnerability pipeline

  • Triage, validate, route, and drive remediation of findings from every source: SAST, DAST, SCA, code review, pentests, and bug bounty

  • Build the automation that removes manual effort from each of those steps

  • External pentests and bug bounty program: set scope, direct the testers, judge severity, and close the loop

Making bug classes go away

  • Spot the patterns across findings and remove the root cause, not just the instance

  • Set the secure patterns and defaults that make the right way the easy way

  • Write custom static analysis rules for our own anti-patterns, so a fixed bug class stays fixed

  • Review platform-layer controls (authorization, service identity, secrets handling, gateway enforcement), find the gaps, and push the owning teams until they are closed

  • Work alongside engineers on fixes that are simple, get adopted, and hold

Also part of the job

  • Hands-on testing of our applications and APIs, and manual code review of high-exposure services, with depth in authorization and business logic

  • Threat modeling on new and high-exposure designs

  • Security enablement across engineering, including a security champions program

What we're looking for

  • Vulnerability management, automated. Experience running vulnerability management end to end, and automating it with code against scanner, ticketing, and source-control APIs

  • An engineering background. You have shipped and maintained real software. You read unfamiliar code quickly, review it rigorously, and reason about architecture and failure modes.

  • Ownership to done. You take problems all the way through, including fixes that depend on other teams. You follow up on the fix you recommended three sprints ago.

  • Judgment over tenure. We care more about the depth of your judgment than your years of experience.

  • Code auditing in at least one of Go, Python, Node.js, Ruby, or Java, and the willingness to work in the rest

  • Practical command of the OWASP Top 10, with real depth in broken access control and business logic flaws

  • SAST, DAST, and SCA in CI/CD, tuned so engineers trust the output. Cloud fundamentals on GCP or AWS. Docker and Kubernetes.

  • You separate real findings from theoretical ones.

  • You disagree in the open, with evidence, and update when someone brings better evidence.

  • Your influence travels asynchronously, across time zones, to people with strong opinions and no reporting line to you.

Bonus

  • Scaling security tooling across many repositories, languages, and build systems

  • Prior experience writing custom static analysis rules (Semgrep, CodeQL, or similar)

  • Fintech, payments, or other environments under serious third-party security review (PCI DSS, SOC 2, customer audits)

  • Fully distributed, asynchronous engineering experience

  • Offensive experience in whatever form you found it. Pentesting on web, API, mobile, or cloud is the most directly relevant. Hardware and embedded work, physical security and lock sport, red team engagements, protocol and radio work, and CTF or bug bounty results all count.

  • Advanced offensive certifications. OSWE and BSCP are the most relevant; CPTS, CRTO, and similar also count.

  • Public work: research, tooling, disclosures, talks

Benefits we offer:

  • Generous compensation in cash and equity

  • Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested

  • Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture

  • Flexible paid time off and Year-end break

  • Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - US and Canada specific

  • 4% matching in 401k / RRSP - US and Canada specific

  • MacBook Pro delivered to your door

  • One-time stipend to set up a home office — desk, chair, screen, etc.

  • Monthly meal stipend

  • Monthly social meet-up stipend

  • Annual health and wellness stipend

  • Annual Learning stipend

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Who we are:

About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team
Stripe offers an interesting middle ground between joining a small startup and going to work for a multinational company. We have systems and processes optimized for early-career professionals. You will be in an environment that prizes rigor, discipline, and reliability—from our products, from our ways of working, and from our colleagues. You will learn how the best teams put together extremely reliable systems, and you will be responsible for operating these systems, with adequate backup when things get tough.
The Security organization is dedicated to building and maintaining a secure financial infrastructure platform. By joining this team, you will be on the front lines, engineering solutions that protect the sensitive data and systems underpinning a huge portion of the world's economy. You will contribute to core security functions like threat detection and rapid incident response, building and scaling the platforms that manage vulnerabilities, and proactively performing offensive security assessments to identify weaknesses before they can be exploited. This is a chance to apply software engineering principles and new technologies such as AI to solve complex, high-stakes security challenges, ultimately ensuring that Stripe's mission to increase the GDP of the internet is achieved securely.

What you’ll do
As a Security Engineer New Grad you will have the opportunity to work across various security disciplines and own projects from start to finish. Your work will focus on securing Stripe's complex environment by applying software engineering principles to security challenges.
  • You will learn and apply the principles of secure-by-default design by working closely with product and infrastructure engineering teams.
  • You'll develop a foundational understanding of various security domains, such as threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, or offensive security.
  • You'll learn to act as a security subject matter expert, tailoring answers to both engineers and non-engineers.
  • You'll contribute to the development of internal tools and automation to scale security efforts across Stripe.
  • You will participate in threat modeling discussions, learning to balance security requirements with product advancement and user experience.
Responsibilities
  • Work on cross-functional projects, directly collaborating with other engineers
  • Give meaningful feedback on code reviews and technical designs
  • Contribute to our overall security posture by continuously improving security processes, tooling, and defenses.
  • Develop a deep understanding of Stripe’s security primitives, frameworks, and invariants.
  • Provide actionable insights to help identify, prevent, detect, and respond to anomalous or potentially malicious activity.
Who you are:
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements
  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s program in Computer Science or related field (graduating by Summer 2026)
  • Some experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Java, Ruby, Python, JavaScript, Scala, and Go. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present
  • Experience from either previous internships or working collaboratively on multi-person coding projects (in a university or professional setting)
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts
  • Aptitude to think like an attacker and reason through different approaches to reducing security risk.
Preferred qualifications
  • Experience in code review practices, and an understanding of how to safely update production systems
  • Familiarity with navigating and managing work in large code bases
  • Prior experience or course work in cyber security, digital forensics, or incident response (e.g., through log analysis or capture-the-flag events).
  • Familiarity with foundational security concepts such as the OWASP Top 10 web application vulnerabilities.
  • Basic knowledge of SQL or experience analyzing medium to large data sets.
  • Exposure to cloud computing platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • An adversarial mindset, understanding the goals, behaviors, and TTPs (tactics, techniques, and procedures) of threat actors.
